title: Genji monogatari tama no ogushi (The Jeweled Comb of The Tale of Genji)

access.edition_or_version: Motoori Norinaga zenshu vol. 4, ed. Ono Susumu, Chikuma Shobo, 1969
access.language_used: ja (via scholarly quotation and English translation)

tone_mechanisms_observed: theorizes mono no aware as the emotional core of literature
locates the profoundest aware in the emotion that arises when events do not go as one desires
treats sensitivity to transience as a virtue, not a weakness
models a tender, non-despairing relation to impermanence
mechanics.emotional_progression: Not a narrative work; the commentary's argument moves from definition of aware to its centrality in Genji to a defense of feeling.
mechanics.point_of_view: Critical/theoretical voice, part of the kokugaku (national learning) movement.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Prose commentary; not directly a stylistic exemplar, but the source of the concept.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Advocates neither indulgence nor suppression but a moved attention to things.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Nativist literary theory grounded in Buddhist impermanence. Verified indirectly through peer-reviewed scholarship and SEP; direct inspection of the Japanese edition is an open verification gap.
mechanics.copyright_note: Modern collected-works edition copyrighted; analytical paraphrase only.
